questions.explanation_en: Statement 1 is correct — Parliament (through Presidential orders) can make laws for the State under President's Rule. Statement 2 is incorrect — President's Rule can be extended beyond 6 months with Parliamentary approval every 6 months, even without a national emergency.

questions.question_en: Which of the following are NOT necessarily the consequences of the proclamation of the President's rule in a State? 1. Dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly; 2. Removal of the Council of Ministers in the State; 3. Dissolution of the local bodies
questions.topic: President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.language_status: English structured extraction; Telugu not included in index
questions.explanation_en: When President's Rule is proclaimed: the State Legislature is suspended/dissolved (or kept under suspended animation), and the Council of Ministers is removed. Local bodies (municipalities, panchayats) are NOT necessarily dissolved. So 1 (dissolution may not be immediate) and 3 (local bodies not affected) are not necessary consequences.
